principles.rule: Use the Ubiquitous Language: name classes, methods, and modules with the domain's terms so code, conversation, and docs share one vocabulary.
checks: no technical aliases for domain concepts

principles.rule: Isolate domain logic in its own layer, free of UI, persistence, and infrastructure concerns.
checks: no SQL/HTTP/framework code in domain objects
domain layer has no outward dependencies

principles.rule: Distinguish Entities (defined by identity/continuity) from Value Objects (defined by attributes); make Value Objects immutable.
checks: entities have stable identity, not attribute-equality

principles.rule: Model Aggregates with a single root as the consistency and access boundary; external references go only to the root; enforce invariants within the boundary.
checks: external code references only aggregate roots

principles.rule: Use Repositories (collection-like, for aggregate roots only) and Factories (for complex creation) to keep persistence and construction out of domain logic.
checks: repositories exist only for aggregate roots

principles.rule: Aim for supple design: intention-revealing interfaces, side-effect-free functions, explicit assertions, and making implicit concepts explicit.
Define explicit Bounded Contexts where the model and language are consistent; protect boundaries with an Anticorruption Layer when integrating other models.
Identify and focus effort on the Core Domain; separate generic subdomains and supporting code from the differentiating core.
checks: core domain clearly identified and prioritized
